name: Blacksmith (GitHub Actions runners)

modes.label: macOS M4 runners, per minute
modes.note: $0.08/min for 6 vCPU (pricing page). 12 vCPU = $0.16/min derived from the docs' billing rule (macOS 6 vCPU minute = 20 x64-2vCPU minutes, scaling with vCPU).

modes.label: Windows Server 2025 runners (public beta), per minute
modes.note: $0.008/min for 2 vCPU (pricing page); docs: 'The same conversion rate applies proportionally to runners with higher vCPU counts' (4 vCPU = $0.016/min, etc.).

modes.label: Ubuntu x64 runners, per minute
modes.note: CI runner. Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). https://www.blacksmith.sh/pricing: Ubuntu x64 $0.004/min (per 2 vCPU, proportional to vCPU per docs); 3,000 free minutes/month. $0.004/min per 2 vCPU, proportional to vCPU (docs).

modes.label: Ubuntu ARM runners, per minute
modes.note: CI runner. Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). https://www.blacksmith.sh/pricing: Ubuntu ARM $0.0025/min (2 vCPU), assumed proportional to vCPU like x64; sizes mirror x64 (not verified for arm). 3,000 free minutes/month shared.

modes.label: Testbox (agent dev VM on x64 runner rates, early beta)
modes.note: Early beta. Warm microVM launched via a GitHub Actions workflow; the agent syncs a local tree over rsync/SSH and runs commands. Default idle timeout 30 min (configurable), billed per minute at CI runner pricing (x64 sizes shown; ARM at ARM runner rates).

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.note: 3,000 free x64-2vCPU minutes/month per org (= $12), consumable on Windows (2x) and macOS (20x per 6 vCPU) runners.

caveats: GitHub Actions runners only: jobs must be triggered by workflows; not a general agent sandbox.
Per-minute rounding assumed (GitHub job minutes); not explicitly stated.
Sticky disks / Docker layer cache $0.50/GB-month; static IPs $100/IP/month (Windows/Ubuntu).
macOS capacity and regions not published.
ARM prices for 4-32 vCPU ($0.005-$0.04/min) and macOS 12 vCPU ($0.16/min) are shown directly on the pricing page vCPU selector.
Blacksmith Sandboxes (full-VM sandboxes for coding agents with environment snapshots) is waitlist-only beta with no published price; not encoded.
Sticky disks / Docker layer cache ($0.50/GB-month, metered hourly) are auto-evicted after 7 days without use. actions/cache is free: 25 GB per repo per week, LRU eviction.

fleet.verification: Pricing advertises no card required to try.
fleet.notes: Official blog advertises no concurrency limits, scaling to hundreds of jobs/thousands of vCPUs; pricing also offers enterprise concurrency. No finite new-account cap, verification details or review SLA published; null denotes unquantified/unbounded advertised allowance, not zero.

snapshot_auto.quote: After a job completes, the microVM is destroyed, along with any of its state.
snapshot_auto.note: Runner VMs are ephemeral. Only opt-in sticky disks (incl. Docker layer cache) are committed as a new disk snapshot at job end ('Once the job completes, the sticky disk will be unmounted and committed for future invocations'); that is persistent-cache disk state, not machine state, and no memory.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: After a job completes, the microVM is destroyed, along with any of its state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot API for runners/Testboxes in the docs. The waitlist-only 'Blacksmith Sandboxes' beta advertises 'Fully managed environment snapshots ... to boot sandboxes from' (https://www.blacksmith.sh/sandboxes), unpriced and undocumented; not counted.

harness_api.quote: Install the [code]smith app via Slack ... Mention @codesmith on any PR in any GitHub repo that Blacksmith is connected to. ... Open the Web UI to directly message [code]smith.
harness_api.note: Blacksmith's own background coding agent [code]smith ($1.75/agent compute unit) is driven only via web UI, Slack, GitHub mentions and Linear; no documented public API/SDK to start/stream/resume sessions. Testbox CLI (early beta) is the reverse direction: a local agent runs commands (rsync + exec) in a CI microVM - generic exec, not a harness API.

ingress_rules.quote: SSH access is opt-in and must be enabled by a GitHub organization admin ... Only the GitHub user who triggered the job can SSH into the runner
ingress_rules.note: CI runners expose no user ports/URLs (no inbound HTTPS). The only inbound path is the opt-in debug SSH port, gated by an org-level toggle and the triggering user's GitHub SSH keys; no user-configurable IP allowlists, security groups or port exposure.

guest_firewall.note: Jobs run in Firecracker microVMs with their own kernel ('Our jobs never share kernels', security page) and GitHub-runner-style sudo/root; iptables/nftables inside should work. Not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: Testboxes sync your local changes to a Blacksmith microVM and run commands inside a real GitHub Actions job, with access to secrets, OIDC tokens, and service containers.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are ordinary GitHub Actions secrets/OIDC tokens exposed to the job inside the VM; no credential-injecting proxy documented. [code]smith MCP connector credentials are stored per user/org for MCP servers (not an outbound HTTP proxy for the sandbox).

volume_attach.quote: Each sticky disk is hot-loaded into the runner and mounted at the specified path. The sticky disk is formatted as an ext4 filesystem.
volume_attach.note: Sticky disks: Ceph-backed ext4 block devices keyed by name, up to 5 per job, $0.50/GB-month, evicted after 7 days unused. Docker layer cache uses the same mechanism. Persistence is snapshot-clone-commit per job, not a live attached volume.

volume_shared.quote: Every job always works on its own isolated clone of the sticky disk — jobs never share a live disk, and a job's writes only become visible to future runs if its clone is committed as the new snapshot when the job completes.
volume_shared.note: Many concurrent jobs can hydrate from the same sticky-disk snapshot (read-write private clone each), last commit wins; not a shared live filesystem. Optional branch protection limits which jobs can commit.
